title: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction
abstract: arXiv:2610.16615v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual token compression has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the inference cost of Vision-Language Models. Existing methods select tokens based on text relevance, visual diversity, or a fixed combination of both---treating the relevance-diversity balance as a universal constant independent of the input. We conduct a systematic analysis to challenge this assumption. At the dataset level, grid-searching the optimal relevance-diversity weight per benchmark reveals substantial cross-task variation. More critically, we further maximize per-sample answer likelihood to recover sample-level oracle weights, finding that their distributions not only differ markedly across benchmarks but also exhibit high within-benchmark variance. Based on these observations, we propose SAVER, a framework for Sample-Aware relevance-diversity balanced Visual tokEn Reduction. translated_title: 当1+1适得其反：重新思考面向样本感知的视觉Token缩减中的相关性-多样性平衡
translated_abstract: 视觉Token压缩已成为降低视觉语言模型推理成本的关键技术。现有方法基于文本相关性、视觉多样性或两者的固定组合来选择Token——将相关性-多样性的平衡视为与输入无关的通用常数。我们通过系统性分析来挑战这一假设。在数据集层面，对每个基准测试网格搜索最优的相关性-多样性权重，揭示了显著的跨任务差异。更关键的是，我们进一步通过最大化每个样本的答案似然来恢复样本级的最优权重，发现其分布不仅在基准测试之间差异明显，而且在同一基准测试内部也表现出高方差。基于这些观察，我们提出了SAVER——一个样本感知的相关性-多样性平衡视觉Token缩减框架。我们首先从空间集中度导出几何意图先验（GIP）……
tldr: 本文通过系统分析揭示视觉Token缩减中相关性-多样性的最优权重应随输入样本动态变化而非固定常数，并据此提出样本感知的SAVER框架以实现更优的Token压缩。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that the optimal relevance-diversity balance for visual token reduction varies substantially across individual samples rather than being a universal constant, and proposes SAVER, a sample-aware framework that adaptively balances relevance and diversity for each input.
